title: 1994 South African general election
summary: Between 26 and 29 April 1994 South Africans of all races voted in the first national and provincial elections held under universal franchise, run under the Interim Constitution. The ANC won about 62.6 percent of the vote and 252 of 400 National Assembly seats, and on 9 May the Assembly elected Nelson Mandela president.

uncertainty.note: The Library of Congress gives 26-29 April 1994 as the voting period; the O'Malley Archive says only April 1994. The record ID uses 27 April, which was not confirmed on an opened page. Vote shares vary slightly by source (62.6 percent here).

where.modern_name: South Africa, nationwide (pin at Pretoria, seat of government)
where.historical_name: South Africa under the Interim Constitution, national and provincial ballots

importance.justification: The first democratic election ended white-minority rule and installed Nelson Mandela as South Africa's first Black president.

related.because: The 1990-94 negotiations that ended apartheid produced the Interim Constitution and its universal franchise.

sources.title: The 1994 Elections
sources.publisher: The O'Malley Archives, Nelson Mandela Foundation

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date label: sources give a four-day voting window, while the record ID says 27 April. The pin is symbolic, as the election was nationwide.
